title: pcapng: Fix an integer overflow and some error-path memory leaks.
description:
Catch an integer overflow in pcapng_read_block which could lead to an attempt
to allocate 4 GBytes of memory.

Calling wtap_block_add_string_option_owned without checking the return value
means that the caller can not possibly know who now owns the string that was
passed in -- unless the caller is ABSOLUTELY sure that the call can never ever
fail.  This seems worthy of making it a G_GNUC_WARN_UNUSED_RESULT (or
WS_WARN_UNUSED), so let's do that.  Fix the callsites so that they all check
the return value, and at least free the string (and ignore the failure) when
the string can not be added.

Fix a sundry error-path memory leak in pcapng_read_name_resolution_block.

Fix incorrect error text in pcapng_process_if_descr_block_option.


(cherry picked from commit a6488441f7427aef6b7e4c04d791a64eb6429cde)

Co-authored-by: Darius Davis <darius-wireshark@free-range.com.au>

changes_data.diff:
@@ -884,11 +884,12 @@ wtap_block_add_string_option(wtap_block_t block, unsigned option_id, const char
  * @param[in] block Block to which to add the option
  * @param[in] option_id Identifier value for option
  * @param[in] value Value of option
- * @return wtap_opttype_return_val - WTAP_OPTTYPE_SUCCESS if successful,
- * error code otherwise
+ * @return wtap_opttype_return_val - WTAP_OPTTYPE_SUCCESS if successful (caller no longer owns @p value),
+ * error code otherwise (caller still owns @p value)
+ * @note To avoid memory leaks, the caller @b must examine the return status to determine ownership of @p value.
  */
 WS_DLL_PUBLIC wtap_opttype_return_val
-wtap_block_add_string_option_owned(wtap_block_t block, unsigned option_id, char *value);
+wtap_block_add_string_option_owned(wtap_block_t block, unsigned option_id, char *value) G_GNUC_WARN_UNUSED_RESULT;
